observation: No detection above 0.25, despite visible damage on the upper lug and left edge.
hypothesis: The damage spans several disconnected mask components and scales. Limited pose/defect examples may leave this appearance uncovered; this is a hypothesis, not an observed internal cause.

observation: A bent prediction at confidence 0.420 covers only part of the upper-edge defect; IoU is 0.486, below the fixed 0.5 matching cutoff.
hypothesis: The box follows the visually strongest notch but underestimates the annotated extent. This demonstrates why finding a defect-looking region is not sufficient for correct localization.

observation: The dark blue patch beside the inner ring has no prediction above the operating threshold.
hypothesis: The relatively small, dark patch blends into the inner-rim shadow and metallic texture. More representative dark-color flaws and higher-resolution validation are plausible next experiments.

observation: The red patch is correctly detected as color at confidence 0.878, but two bent boxes and a second color box remain as false positives.
hypothesis: The same high-contrast region triggers multiple class heads. Class-aware NMS intentionally keeps different classes; partial boxes also escape same-class suppression. This is classification and duplicate-counting failure, not a missed red patch.

observation: The upper scratch is matched at confidence 0.307, but higher-scoring color (0.753) and bent (0.614) boxes overlap it. The separate lower-left scratch is missed.
hypothesis: A dark scar can resemble staining or deformation, while the second scar has different orientation and local texture. The pattern suggests class ambiguity and incomplete coverage across multiple defects.
